# r4.5

- Reduces the metadata round trips before remote downloads and Explorer drag-and-drop copies. Shared parent directories are checked once per inventory, and attributes already supplied by directory listings are reused. Missing attributes are fetched only where needed.
- Keeps paint, timer and application/COM messages moving while Windows requests drag metadata, without consuming the mouse-release or Escape input that belongs to the drag operation.
- Preserves the underlying remote-read error in Nearly instead of replacing every failure with a generic message. A Windows disk-read error can also represent remote metadata, network or timeout failures.
- Handles directory listings that omit owner IDs without falsely rejecting unchanged files during stream reads. File size, modification time and file-type checks remain in place.

## Verification and limits

Generated localhost SFTP tests reduced LSTAT requests for a 100-file tree from 460 to 4; directory-listing requests are separate. Tests cover incomplete listing attributes, unsupported/symlink paths and actual virtual-stream reads. Windows tests cover message dispatch, preserving drag input and cross-process COM reads. This is not a claim that complete downloads are 115 times faster.

Actual Explorer Drop/Escape gestures and a real-server throughput comparison have not been qualified for this change. No improvement against WinSCP timing is claimed. Source files are retained; Explorer continues to manage destination conflicts and partial output.

Stable release, replacing r4.4 as Latest. Uses the existing application registration, settings and normal updater channel.
